bull_case_summary: Netflix has FX-neutral revenue growth and positive operating economics. Round two distinguishes a longer-horizon earnings thesis from a surprise catalyst, while retaining content-adjusted owner cash as the purchase gate.
bear_case_summary: The bear accepts that in-line results alone cannot defeat a purchase thesis. Its stronger objection is the missing bridge from accounting earnings to cash after content commitments, debt and competition risk, with no confirmed bottom or matched cash valuation.
key_points_of_agreement: Present profitable demand is independent of a guidance surprise or currency boost.
Operating margin does not establish owner cash after content obligations.
Annual guidance is prospective and oversold RSI is not a bottom.
key_points_of_disagreement: How far current earnings-based merit advances a prospective purchase before content-adjusted cash and price compensation are verified.
unresolved_uncertainties: Debt, FCF and current/future content obligations.
Sustainable owner cash and competition economics.
Matched valuation and delivery of annual forecasts without assuming price recovery.
